title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-03-01
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Mostly soundboard recording with rough audience intro, but a stellar 1970 show featuring Big Boy Pete, the Cryptical‑Other One sequence and standout harp work.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a classic early‑70s Dead set – the rare Big Boy Pete, an incendiary Cryptical > Other One stretch, tight Good Lovin' drums and a beautiful China Cat > I Know You Rider.  The middle of the show sounds clear on soundboard, though the first two tracks (and a few seconds later) suffer from audience‑mic bleed, high vocal levels and occasional harp overload that benefit from EQ.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars, praising the performance despite mixed comments about early‑show recording flaws; the average rating is ~4.25.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First two songs (and a couple seconds of the third) are from audience mics and sound muddy; vocal mix sits too high in the mid‑section, harp can be overly forward, tape breaks near the end.  The bulk of the set is clear, balanced and benefits from modest EQ.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows naturally with a rare early Big Boy Pete, the powerful Cryptical‑Other One transition that mirrors a New Orleans show, then into Black Peter for the first time in this run, followed by smooth segues into Good Lovin', Dew and the classic China Cat → I Know You Rider.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is solid overall; a few reviewers note it could be a hair louder but his tone shines on the jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ/keyboard work is fine, though some feel the guitar/organ lines on The Other One don’t ‘explode’ as they should. Pigpen’s harp is praised for its musicality but occasionally sits too high in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Good Lovin' drums receive specific praise; overall drum sound is considered tight and lively.
